agree.reason: The nurse's-office numbers and the careful line on graduation would move a sympathetic parent, but a board member weighing $180,000 and the after-dark practices gets values talk and a to-do list, not answers that would change a resisting vote.

honest.reason: The piece rightly declines to promise a higher graduation rate, but it adds things the brief doesn't support: the eight-to-ten-hour sleep need, the biology of the teenage body clock, students who 'almost always' say they're exhausted, 'failed first-period classes,' and the claim that the other district 'faced the same issues.'

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the figures into useful forms: 640 of 890 becomes 'nearly three out of four,' 84% becomes 'one in six don't finish,' and first-period visits are set against second and third combined. It never gives the 65-minute gap, the cost per student, or what one point of attendance would mean here.

right_comparison.reason: Keeping the 7:25 start is shown concretely through the nurse's-office pattern and the AAP gap, but nothing shows whether things are getting worse or holding steady, so the reader sees a snapshot rather than a trend.

qualification.reason: The hedge 'won't fix that by itself' is honest but gives the reader nothing to check: no target for tardies, attendance or graduation, no date to review it, and nothing that happens if the results don't come.

objections.reason: It names all three objections fairly and offers plausible fixes for drop-offs and athletics, but the bus cost gets only a 'what we value' answer, and the fixes rest partly on an invented claim about how the other district handled the same problems.

fit.reason: It has the right op-ed shape, with a headline, a first-person voice, a call to the April 14 meeting and a byline, and at roughly 650 words it sits right at the limit.
